Reluctant to stand up, I shrunk lower down to the ground as I replied, 'Yes, O Rasulullaah ﷺ When I stood .up, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'Something has happened amongst the enemy. I want you to bring me some information from them.' Although I was the most frightened at the time and feeling the coldest, I left. Rasulullaah ﷺ then prayed, 'O Allaah! Protect him from the front, from the back, from the right, from the left, from above and from beneath."' Hadhrat Hudhayfa (RA) says, "I swear by Allaah, that (after this du'aa) every bit ( 1 ) Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya. of fear and cold in me then left and I experienced none of it. As I left, Rasulullaah instructed, 'O Hudhayfa! Do not do anything amongst them until you return.' When I drew close to the enemy army, noticed the light of a fire that they had lit. There I saw a large dark-skinned man warming his hands at the fire and rubbing them on his sides as he said, 'Let us leave! Let us leave!' I had not known Abu Sufyaan before this. I removed an arrow with a white feather from my quiver and placed it on my bow to fire at him in the light when I recalled the instruction of Rasulullaah ﷺ 'Do not do anything amongst them until you return.' I then restrained myself and put the arrow back into the quiver. I then gathered my courage and proceeded amongst the army."

"The closest people to me was the Banu Aamir tribe who were announcing, 'O family of Aamir! Leave! Leave! You cannot stay here!' The wind was raging within their ranks without blowing even a hand's span outside their quarters. By Allaah! I could hear the sounds of rocks smashing against their carriages and beddings as the wind threw them up. I then left to return to Rasulullaah ﷺ. When I had reached halfway or close to halfway, I met approximately twenty horsemen all wearing turbans. They said to me, 'Inform your leader that Allaah has acted on his behalf.'"

"When I returned to Rasulullaah ﷺ, I found him performing salaah wrapped in a small shawl. By Allaah! The cold returned to me as soon as I returned and I started shivering. While performing salaah, Rasulullaah ﷺ motioned me with his hand. When I drew closer to him, he put the edge of the shawl on me. It was the practice of Rasulullaah ﷺ to perform salaah whenever anything worried him. I then informed Rasulullaah ﷺ about what had happened and told him the enemy were leaving when I left them. It was then that Allaah revealed the following verses of the Qur'aan: jk gn.n.t Jul ijj Ujy uysrj O you who have Imaan! Remember Allaah's favour (to you) when the armies approached you, against which We sent (in your defence) a (fierce) wind and troops (of angels) that you could not see (thus causing fear in the hearts of the enemy, causing them to retreat). Allaah is Watchful over what you do' ... (Afterwards,) Allaah returned the Kuffaar (to Makkah) with their fury without them achieving any good (without them attaining their objective of destroying Islaam and the Muslims). Allaah suffices for the Mu'mineen in battle (causing them to defeat the Kuffaar despite their lack of physical resources). Allaah is Omnipotent, Mighty (and none can fight Him). (Surah Ahzaab, verses 9-25)
sources: Haakim and Bayhaqi (Vol.9 Pg.148) as quoted in Al Bidaaya wan Nihaaya (Vol.4 Pg.l 14). Abu Dawood and ibn Asaakir have also reported the Hadith in detail as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.279).

paras: Hadhrat Yazeed Taymi narrates that they were with Hadhrat Hudhayfa (RA) when someone asked him, "Had I met Rasulullaah ﷺ, I would have fought fiercely and sacrificed my life." Hadhrat Hudhayfa (RA) said, "Would you really have? 1 saw a time when we were with Rasulullaah ﷺ during the Battle of Ahzaab. There blew that night an extremely violent and icy wind. Rasulullaah then announced, 'The person who will go and gather intelligence about the enemy, Allaah shall make him my companion on the Day of Qiyaamah."' The rest of the Hadith is similar to the narration of Abdul Azeez quoted above. This narration however, quotes that Hadhrat Hudhayfa (RA) said, "When 1 returned to Rasulullaah ﷺ, the cold struck me as soon as I arrived and I shivered. When I informed Rasulullaah ﷺ about events, he covered me with the extra part of the shawl he was performing salaah in. I then slept until dawn. When dawn arrived, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'Wake up, O sleepy head."
sources: Muslim. (3) ibn is'haaq reporting from Muhammad bin Ka'b Qurazi. (4) ibn Is'haaq as quoted in Al Bidaaya wan Nihaaya (Vol.4 Pg.49) (5) lbnSa'd(Vol.3Pg.2l).

paras: Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ announced, "Who will go and see what the enemy is doing and return (with the news)?" Rasulullaah ﷺ stipulated that the person will return and added, "I shall make du'aa to Allaah that he should be my companion in Jannah." However, no one stood up because of the intense fear, hunger and cold that everyone was suffering.

Hadhrat Abu Saa'ib (RA) narrates that a man from the Banu Abdul Ash'hal tribe reported, "My brother and I participated in the Battle of Uhud and we both returhed wounded. When Rasulullaah ﷺ's caller announced that we should march in pursuit of the enemy, I said to my brother or he said to me, 'Can we miss this opportunity to march with Rasulullaah ﷺ By Allaah! Although we had no transport to ride and were both heavily wounded, we went with Rasulullaah ﷺ. Since my wounds were less serious than my brother's, I carried him when he could not manage and he walked at other times. In this manner, we eventually reached the place where the other Muslims were."

Another narration states that it was Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Sahl (RA) and his brother Hadhrat Raafi bin Sahl (RA) who proceeded to Hamraa'ul Asad in a wounded condition and without transport as the one carried the other.

Several elders of the Banu Salma tribe have reported that Hadhrat Amr bin Jamooh was badly crippled while his four sons were like lions and participated in every battle by the side. When the Battle of Uhud took place, his sons tried to prevent him from participating saying, "Allaah has excused you." He then approached Rasulullaah gjj3i!r saying, "My sons want to stop me from leaving with you to participate in this battle. By Allaah! I wish to walk in Jannah with my paralysis." Rasulullaah ﷺ said to him, "Allaah has excused you. Jihaad is not compulsory for you." Rasulullaah ﷺ then said to his sons, "You need not prevent him (from participating) because Allaah may perhaps grant him the high rank of martyrdom." Hadhrat Amr bin Jamooh (RA) then left with Rasulullaah ﷺ and was martyred during the Battle of Uhud.
sources: Ibn Is'haaq as quoted in Al Bidaaya wan Nihaaya (Vol. 4 Pg.37).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Qataadah (RA) who participated in the Battle of Uhud says that Hadhrat Amr bin Jamooh (RA) who was crippled once approached Rasulullaah and said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ If I fight in the path of Allaah and am killed, will I walk with a healthy leg in Jannah?" "Certainly,' replied Rasulullaah ﷺ. Subsequently, the Kuffaar martyred Hadhrat Amr bin Jamooh (RA), his nephew and their slave during the Battle of Uhud. When Rasulullaah ﷺ passed by (the corpse of) Hadhrat Amr bin Jamooh (RA), he said, "I can see him walking in Jannah with a healthy leg." Rasulullaah ﷺ then instructed that Hadhrat Amr bin Jamooh, his nephew and slave should be buried in one grave.
sources: Ahmad. Haythami (Vol Pg.315) has commented on the chain of narrators. Bayhaqi (Vol.9 Pg.24) has also reported the narration.

paras: Hadhrat Yahya bin Abdul Hameed' narrates from his grandfather that an arrow struck Hadhrat Raafi bin Khadeej (RA) during either the Battle of Uhud or the Battle of. He then went to Rasulullaah ﷺ and asked him to remove the arrow. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "O Raafi! If you want, I could remove the shaft together with arrowhead. Otherwise, I could remove only the shaft without arrowhead and testify on the Day of Qiyaamah that you are a martyr." Hadhrat Raafi said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ ! Remove the shaft without the arrowhead and testify for me on the Day of Qiyaamah that I am a martyr." Rasulullaah ﷺ did this. Hadhrat Raafi (RA) lived until the period when Hadhrat Mu'aawiya was Khalifah, when the wound reopened and he passed away after Asr. Such is the report according to this narration. However, the correct version of the story according to Al Bidaaya wan Nihaaya is that Hadhrat Raafi bin Khadeej passed away after the Khilaafah of Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA). isaaba (Vol. 1 Pg.496) states that a period elapsed between the time his wound reopened and the time that he passed away. Several such Ahadeeth shall Insha Allaah be quoted in the chapter discussing patience.
sources: One of narrators Amr bin Marzooq is unsure which battle it was.
